candidate.answerReason: The four equal sectors on the left contain two odd and two even numbers. The three equal sectors on the right contain two odd and one even number. Exactly 6 of the 12 equally likely sector pairs have an even sum.

methods.label: List the pairs with even sums
methods.explanation:
A sum is even exactly when both numbers are odd or both are even. The left wheel has numbers \(3,5,8,4\) in four equal sectors, and the right wheel has \(6,9,7\) in three equal sectors.

With fair, independent spins, each left sector can be paired with each of the three right sectors, giving \(4\cdot3=12\) equally likely outcomes. Write each pair with the left-wheel number first. The pairs with both numbers odd are
\[
(3,9),\ (3,7),\ (5,9),\ (5,7).
\]
The pairs with both numbers even are
\[
(8,6),\ (4,6).
\]
These lists include every same-parity pair exactly once, and the two lists cannot overlap. Thus \(6\) of the \(12\) outcomes have even sums, giving probability
\[
\frac{6}{12}=\boxed{\frac12},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
